findings.summary: H1's row check refuses only a line feed. A carriage return, which CommonMark treats as a line ending, passes, so a record whose H1 adds a heading or a table row inside section 5.3 is still accepted by check_record. README lines 37-38 ('neither its current nor its new text may hold a line break ... so it cannot add a row, a column or a heading') and the HS53 brief item 1 ('with a line break in its current or new text') claim more than the model enforces.
findings.evidence: Mutations run with check_record on the published record and the pinned HS43 bytes, with E3 re-rendered. ACCEPTED: H1 proposed = published proposed + CR (U+000D) + '## 99. Injected heading' (no LF, still two unescaped pipes). ACCEPTED: H1 proposed = published proposed + CR + 'INJECTED'. With the items applied, the local markdown-it-py 4.2.0 (commonmark preset plus the table rule, offline) renders the first as an h2 '99. Injected heading' after a table cut to the SERVER and OBSERVER rows (BROKER to HOST_CONTAINMENT fall out of the table), and the second as a new table row 'INJECTED' between OBSERVER and BROKER. The published spec holds no CR and renders all seven rows. Refused, correctly: LF plus a new row, an extra cell, a trailing LF in current, H1 in the SERVER row, CR plus a pipe-led row (cell count). Cause: lines 278-280 test only for LF in current and proposed. In check(), only the author-set effective digest stops such a record; the published bytes are correct. Same class as SOL1-5 and SOL2-1. Related aside: _cell (lines 153-154) maps LF but not CR, so a CR in a superseded clause's replacement also renders a heading inside section 13 (accepted by check_record; that is reviewed record content, so advice only). Fix: refuse CR in H1's current and proposed (or require exactly one line by str.splitlines), and map CR in _cell.
